chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and Hisham ibn Salim, and others besides these two, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic:
[48:4] He it is Who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers
He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the faith.'

key_terms.أَنْزَلَ: Sent down; the divine act of bestowing or descending, employed both for Quranic revelation and for spiritual gifts granted by Allah
key_terms.السَّكِينَةَ: Tranquillity; the divine inner peace and serenity sent down by Allah into the hearts of the believers, identified in this hadith as iman itself
key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: Faith; the core theological conviction and belief that constitutes the believer's inner tranquillity
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; a reverential honorific for Allah expressing His absolute power and transcendence
key_terms.غَيْرِهِمَا: Others besides these two; a formula indicating additional unnamed narrators in the sanad alongside the two explicitly named transmitters
key_terms.قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Hearts of the believers; the spiritual locus within which Allah deposits faith and serenity

ai.seo_question: What is the 'tranquillity' (al-sakinah) that Allah sent down into the hearts of the believers according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides an authoritative tafsir of Quran 48:4, equating the divine 'tranquillity' (al-sakinah) sent down into the hearts of the believers with iman (faith) itself. The hadith establishes that the spiritual serenity referenced in Surah al-Fath is not merely a psychological state but is ontologically identical to faith as a theological reality. This concise interpretive statement is characteristic of the Imami tradition of grounding inner spiritual realities in the foundational doctrines of the religion.
